title: Bakery
statementMd:
Masha wants to open her own bakery and bake muffins in one of the $*n*$ cities numbered from $1$ to $*n*$. There are $*m*$ bidirectional roads, each of whose connects some pair of cities.

To bake muffins in her bakery, Masha needs to establish flour supply from some storage. There are only $*k*$ storages, located in different cities numbered $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*k*}$.

Unforunately the law of the country Masha lives in prohibits opening bakery in any of the cities which has storage located in it. She can open it only in one of another $*n* - *k*$ cities, and, of course, flour delivery should be paid — for every kilometer of path between storage and bakery Masha should pay $1$ ruble.

Formally, Masha will pay $*x*$ roubles, if she will open the bakery in some city $*b*$ ($*a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*$ for every $1 ≤ *i* ≤ *k*$) and choose a storage in some city $*s*$ ($*s* = *a*_{*j*}$ for some $1 ≤ *j* ≤ *k*$) and $*b*$ and $*s*$ are connected by some path of roads of summary length $*x*$ (if there are more than one path, Masha is able to choose which of them should be used).

Masha is very thrifty and rational. She is interested in a city, where she can open her bakery (and choose one of $*k*$ storages and one of the paths between city with bakery and city with storage) and pay minimum possible amount of rubles for flour delivery. Please help Masha find this amount.

## Input

The first line of the input contains three integers $*n*$, $*m*$ and $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{5}$, $0 ≤ *k* ≤ *n*$) — the number of cities in country Masha lives in, the number of roads between them and the number of flour storages respectively.

Then $*m*$ lines follow. Each of them contains three integers $*u*$, $*v*$ and $*l*$ ($1 ≤ *u*, *v* ≤ *n*$, $1 ≤ *l* ≤ 10^{9}$, $*u* ≠ *v*$) meaning that there is a road between cities $*u*$ and $*v*$ of length of $*l*$ kilometers .

If $*k* > 0$, then the last line of the input contains $*k*$ distinct integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*k*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) — the number of cities having flour storage located in. If $*k* = 0$ then this line **is not presented in the input**.

## Output

Print the minimum possible amount of rubles Masha should pay for flour delivery in the only line.

If the bakery can not be opened (while satisfying conditions) in any of the $*n*$ cities, print $- 1$ in the only line.

## Note

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ce17d1195580cb7b30943e16e8f7fe3caec0783b.png)Image illustrates the first sample case. Cities with storage located in and the road representing the answer are darkened.
statementZhMd:
Masha 想开一家属于自己的面包店，并在编号为 $*1*$ 到 $*n*$ 的城市中的某一座城市烘焙松饼。城市之间有 $*m*$ 条双向道路，每条道路连接某一对城市。

为了在面包店烘焙松饼，Masha 需要从某个仓库建立面粉供应。有且仅有 $*k*$ 个仓库，它们位于编号为 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*k*}$ 的不同城市中。

不幸的是，Masha 所居住国家的法律禁止在有仓库的城市开设面包店。她只能在另外的 $*n* - *k*$ 座城市中的某一座开店。当然，面粉运输需要付费——对于仓库与面包店之间路径的每一公里，Masha 需要支付 1 卢布。

形式化地说，如果 Masha 在某座城市 $*b*$ 开设面包店（对于每个 $1 ≤ *i* ≤ *k*$，均有 $*a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*$），并选择位于某座城市 $*s*$ 的仓库（其中 $*s* = *a*_{*j*}$，且 $1 ≤ *j* ≤ *k*$），同时 $*b*$ 和 $*s*$ 之间存在一条道路总长度为 $*x*$ 的路径（如果路径不止一条，Masha 可以选择其中任意一条使用），那么她将支付 $*x*$ 卢布。

Masha 非常节俭且理性。她想知道在哪座城市开设面包店（并选择 $*k*$ 个仓库中的一个，以及面包店所在城市与仓库所在城市之间的一条路径）时，面粉运输费用可以达到最小。请帮助 Masha 求出这个最小费用。

## 约束条件

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*k*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10^{5}$，$0 ≤ *k* ≤ *n*$），分别表示 Masha 所居住国家的城市数量、城市之间的道路数量以及面粉仓库的数量。

接下来 $*m*$ 行，每行包含三个整数 $*u*$、$*v*$ 和 $*l*$（$1 ≤ *u*, *v* ≤ *n*$，$1 ≤ *l* ≤ 10^{9}$，$*u* ≠ *v*$），表示城市 $*u*$ 和城市 $*v*$ 之间有一条长度为 $*l*$ 千米的道路。

如果 $*k* > 0$，输入的最后一行包含 $*k*$ 个互不相同的整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*k*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$），表示有面粉仓库的城市编号。如果 $*k* = 0$，则输入中**不包含**这一行。

## 输出格式

仅一行输出 Masha 为面粉运输所需支付的最小卢布数。

如果无法在满足条件的任何一座城市中开设面包店，则仅一行输出 $- 1$。

## 说明
